messages:
sara_lopez: Hey team — NimbleHealth POC kickoff is scheduled for Monday. They want a short 2-week Dedicated POC. Asking to provision a dedicated pool with autoscaling and temporary burst credits. Who can own?

mira_chen: I can take the presales config. Need to confirm expected concurrent RPS and token/sec patterns from their app. Jack, can you share rough numbers?

jack_park: From our side: peak ~120 rps for short spikes, steady ~25 rps. Typical generation 200 tokens/request, but they may do 400 for longer summaries. POC will hit ~1k users in waves.

diego_ramos: Ok. For Dedicated POC I'd recommend pool min=2 gpus, target=6, max=12, with burst pool=24 GPUs for short bursts. That maps to continuous throughput and headroom. Also suggest prefix KV cache enabled.

sara_lopez: Can you put that as a config snippet I can share with customer and finance? They asked about pro-rated billing and how bursts are billed.

mira_chen: Sure — sample config: 
```json
{
  "pool_name": "poc-nimble-1",
  "tier": "dedicated",
  "gpu_min": 2,
  "gpu_target": 6,
  "gpu_max": 12,
  "burst_capacity_gpus": 24,
  "burst_window_seconds": 900,
  "kv_cache": true,
  "quant_profile": "int8-safest"
}
```
Billing: bursts are billed at the burst hourly rate while in use, and reserved capacity (min/target) is billed pro-rata for the POC duration. finance-bot will confirm exact numbers.

finance-bot: For a 2-week POC with min=2/target=6 and occasional bursts up to 24 we estimate: base reserved = $X/day (pro-rated), burst usage billed at $Y/hour when consumed. We can send a detailed quote to NimbleHealth sales contact.

jack_park: That sounds fine. One security note: NimbleHealth requires VPC peering for logs and an allowlist of our control plane IPs. They also prefer customer-managed KMS for keys in the POC. Is that possible?

mira_chen: For a short POC we usually provide a temporary API key scoped to the dedicated pool and tighten network controls. Customer-managed KMS in a POC is heavier — can do a short-term exception if legal signs off. Alternatively we can set up a dedicated VPC connector and rotate keys frequently.

diego_ramos: Operationally: I'll create the pool and attach a canary route so we can route 10% of calls initially. Also will enable autoscale policy: scale up if 95th-percentile latency > 350ms for 60s, back down after 5m stable.

deploy-bot: Created pool poc-nimble-1 in us-west-2 with id pool-9523. Canary route "nimble-poc-canary" set to 10% traffic.

sara_lopez: Amazing — thanks Diego + Mira. Jack, I'll send the config + quote. Can we make burst credits available starting Monday morning (PST)?

diego_ramos: I'll ensure burst pool is warm and reserved billing tag applied. Granting burst credits Monday 07:00 PST should be fine.

jack_park: Perfect. One last ask: customer wants telemetry to Datadog and a simple latency dashboard. Can you expose token-level cost by route?

mira_chen: We'll enable the per-route cost tags and forward metrics to their Datadog account with a read-only API key. Need their Datadog ingest token and the monitor IDs they want.

sara_lopez: Noted. I'll collect those and update this thread. Thanks all :thumbsup:

finance-bot: Quote request queued — exporting line items. Expect a PDF by EOD.

sara_lopez: Closing loop — confirmed: pool provisioned, canary live, burst credits scheduled, finance to send quote, security team to review KMS exception if requested. We can re-open if anything breaks.

jack_park: Thanks everyone, excited to get started.
